sentences.text: Aetobarbakinoides brasiliensis is a reptile classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
This animal was a medium-sized aetosaur estimated to reach a total length of about 2 meters.
The known fossils include neck and back vertebrae, ribs, and limb bones such as the scapula, humerus, tibia, and foot bones, with most distinguishing features found in the vertebrae.
It is the first aetosaur diagnosed without osteoderms in its original description, relying instead on vertebral features for identification.
The species is considered one of the oldest known aetosaurs.
The genus is known solely from the holotype specimen CPE2 168, discovered near São Pedro do Sul in the center of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, within the Inhamandá locality.
The genus was first named by Julia B. Desojo, Martin D. Ezcurra, and Edio E. Kischlat in 2012.
The specific name brasiliensis refers to Brazil, where the holotype was found.
Aetobarbakinoides lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
A 2026 study by Ponce, Cerda, and Desojo used histology of limb bones in Aetobarbakinoides brasiliensis to demonstrate diverse growth rates among pseudosuchians.
Only one fossil occurrence of Aetobarbakinoides has been recorded.
Aetobarbakinoides is closely related to the genera Aetosauroides and Neoaetosauroides.
It is debated whether Aetobarbakinoides is more closely related to aetosaurines based on osteoderms or to desmatosuchines based on vertebrae.
